arguments.summary: Fixed-evidence draft: reported AI-infrastructure demand anchors support conditional operating cases for NVDA and MU, but company multiples are stipulated sensitivities rather than observed/fair-value measures, and QQQ’s dated aggregate P/E is not methodologically comparable. NVDA has the strongest supplied 63-session relative path; MU has higher path risk and awaits its FY2026 Q4 result. No directional preference versus QQQ is established.

claims.text: NVDA reported FY2027 first-half GAAP diluted EPS of $4.85; Q2 Data Center revenue was $89.0bn and management guided Q3 revenue to $108.0bn ±2%, excluding China Data Center compute revenue. Broad delivery of that outlook and sustained AI-platform deployment are the operating predicates for the scenario base, while supply/infrastructure constraints, customer funding/deployment delays, or policy friction can interrupt conversion.

NVDA’s FY2027 53-week GAAP sensitivity uses stipulated $9.50/$10.50/$11.50 EPS and 17x/22x/27x P/E cases. Against the September 18 split-adjusted close, results are -27.34%/+3.93%/+39.69%; bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 12.35 percentage points. These are not probabilities, consensus, observed multiples, or a fair-value conclusion.

MU reported FY2026 nine-month GAAP diluted EPS of $41.40 and guided Q4 GAAP EPS to $30.73 ±$1.00, following record Q3 results and high-volume HBM4 shipments. AI-memory demand/pricing and margin conversion are the relevant near-term operating drivers; the annual-period outcome remained provisional pending the scheduled September 30 release.

MU’s ended FY2026 53-week provisional GAAP sensitivity uses stipulated $70.50/$72.50/$74.00 EPS and 10x/14x/18x P/E cases. Against the September 18 split-adjusted close, results are -30.60%/-0.08%/+31.13%; bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by only 0.53 percentage points, so the stipulated stress is near symmetric.

Over matched completed 63-session windows through September 18, NVDA outperformed QQQ by 8.08 percentage points, while MU underperformed QQQ by 7.83 points and QQQ underperformed SPY by 4.59 points. MU’s realized 63-session volatility (89.56%) exceeded NVDA’s (39.63%) and QQQ’s (20.85%). This describes historical path and not future performance or causality.

QQQ’s sponsor profile reported 103 holdings and aggregate P/E of 30.08 as of August 31; its September 18 holdings reported NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%. These dated fund measures establish diversified but material issuer overlap, not current holdings, direct-company valuation equivalence, or fund-level sensitivity to either issuer’s risks.

gaps.description: No observed company P/E, consensus, multiple history, or cross-method valuation framework is supplied. Company P/E inputs are useful explicit stress assumptions but cannot establish fair value, relative cheapness, or a company-versus-QQQ preference.
MU FY2026 Q4 outcome is absent; the supplied record only schedules the September 30 release. This limits the provisional ended-year EPS bridge but not the guidance-conditioned sensitivity.

The policy record is dated and does not quantify issuer revenue, margins, supplier concentration, product applicability, or QQQ loss sensitivity. It supports conditional channels, not a current-policy or quantified-impact conclusion.
No current rate/inflation series or comparable fund operating-demand measure is supplied. Historical technical differences cannot alone establish three-month relative preference.

assumptions: All grid EPS and P/E inputs are stipulated GAAP, constant-diluted-share sensitivities, not consensus, observed multiples, probabilities, or forecasts.
QQQ holdings and aggregate valuation are dated sponsor data and are not interchangeable with company metrics.
The research horizon is 63 sessions; company annual fiscal periods are used only as scenario anchors.
arguments.counter_thesis: Even if reported demand anchors are met, valuation multiples may compress; conversely, stronger AI deployment or memory pricing could exceed the stipulated bull operating cases. The supplied record assigns neither path a probability and does not establish a comparable QQQ operating scenario.

review_conditions.description: Reassess the issuer-versus-QQQ comparison after NVIDIA reports Q3 delivery versus its $108.0bn ±2% revenue outlook and provides Q4 demand/supply commentary; a material shortfall weakens the base residual bridge, while delivery plus sustained deployment supports retesting it.
Reassess MU when FY2026 Q4 GAAP EPS is reported: below, within, or above $30.73 ±$1.00 changes the bear/base/bull residual classification and replaces the provisional annual estimate.
Reassess QQQ overlap and valuation only on a new dated sponsor holdings/characteristics release; changed weights or methodology invalidate use of the current dated look-through.

NVDA.thesis: Reported Q2 FY2027 AI-platform demand and Q3 guidance support a conditional delivery case: Q3 conversion and a sustained 14-week Q4 would support the stipulated annual bridge. NVDA also led QQQ over the supplied 63-session path. Supply commitments, data-center power/capital constraints, and export/supply-chain channels can instead delay revenue conversion.
NVDA.counter_thesis: Guidance delivery does not ensure the stipulated 22x base multiple, and customer infrastructure/capital constraints, China-related policy gates, or Taiwan/South Korea supply disruption could impair conversion. Neither impact magnitude nor likelihood is measured.
assumptions: Scenario EPS/P/E inputs and constant-share residuals are assumptions, not observed valuations or forecasts.

review_conditions.description: Review Q3 results against $108.0bn ±2% revenue outlook and Q4 demand/supply commentary; shortfall weakens the base bridge, delivery supports reassessment.
A split-adjusted completed close below the frozen 50-session average of 214.2726 weakens the historical intermediate-trend component of NVDA’s relative-path observation.

NVDA.valuation: FY2027 is the disclosed 53-week period 2026-01-26 to 2027-01-31. Reported first-half GAAP diluted EPS was $4.85. Bear/base/bull assumed annual GAAP EPS are $9.50/$10.50/$11.50, leaving constant-share residual EPS of $4.65/$5.65/$6.65; base assumes broad Q3-guidance delivery and Q4 demand, while bear/bull assume weaker/stronger conversion. Q3 guidance is revenue/margin/opex—not EPS—and Q4 is 14 weeks. At 17x/22x/27x stipulated P/E, the grid reports -27.34%/+3.93%/+39.69%. Base break-even is $10.1032 EPS holding 22x fixed, or 21.1686x holding $10.50 EPS fixed. Bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 12.35 points; joint EPS/multiple risk and lack of probabilities mean this is sensitivity, not attractiveness.
NVDA.etf_lookthrough: QQQ held NVDA at a dated 8.535228% on September 18; this is not a current fund exposure estimate.

business.conclusion: AI-platform demand and Q3 guidance support a delivery-conditioned bridge.
business.qualification: Supply, infrastructure, and customer-capital constraints can defer conversion.

valuation.conclusion: A fully specified sensitivity grid is available.
valuation.qualification: EPS and multiples are stipulated; no fair-value conclusion follows.

market_behavior.conclusion: NVDA led QQQ over the supplied 63-session window.
market_behavior.qualification: Historical relative strength has no persistence or causal guarantee.

policy_exposure.conclusion: China exclusion and overseas supply reliance identify conditional transmission channels.
policy_exposure.qualification: Current legal status and financial impact are unquantified.

relative_preference.qualification: Technical leadership is insufficient without comparable valuation and forward operating evidence.

MU.thesis: Record Q3 results, guided Q4 EPS, and HBM4 shipments support a conditional AI-memory demand/pricing and margin-conversion case. The base annual residual lies within Q4 guidance, but the FY2026 result remained unreported in this fixed record and MU’s 63-session relative path lagged QQQ with much higher realized volatility.
MU.counter_thesis: A memory demand/pricing or margin reversal, tariff/trade disruption, or Q4 miss would undermine the bridge; even in-line EPS may not preserve the stipulated multiple. Direct policy applicability and impact are unmeasured.
assumptions: FY2026 is a 53-week period ending 2026-09-03 and is a provisional historical estimate pending results.
Scenario EPS/P/E inputs are stipulated constant-share sensitivities.

review_conditions.description: Review the Q4 release against $30.73 ±$1.00 GAAP EPS guidance; it resolves the provisional annual residual and changes the scenario classification.
A split-adjusted completed close below the frozen 50-session average of 927.2569 would weaken the recent rebound reading and reinforce the unresolved 63-session lag.

MU.valuation: FY2026 is the disclosed 53-week period 2025-08-29 to 2026-09-03; it ended before the cutoff, but Q4 results were scheduled for September 30, so this is provisional historical estimation. Reported nine-month GAAP diluted EPS was $41.40. Bear/base/bull assumed annual GAAP EPS are $70.50/$72.50/$74.00, leaving constant-share residuals of $29.10/$31.10/$32.60 versus guided Q4 GAAP EPS of $30.73 ±$1.00: below/within/above the range. At 10x/14x/18x stipulated P/E, the grid reports -30.60%/-0.08%/+31.13%. Base break-even is $72.5571 EPS holding 14x fixed, or 14.0110x holding $72.50 EPS fixed. Bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 0.53 points, near symmetry; joint earnings/multiple risk makes this sensitivity rather than a preference signal.
MU.etf_lookthrough: QQQ held MU at a dated 5.012336% on September 18; this is not current fund exposure.

business.conclusion: Guided Q4 and HBM shipments support an AI-memory demand/pricing bridge.
business.qualification: The Q4 outcome is absent and trade impacts are unmeasured.

valuation.conclusion: A provisional ended-year sensitivity is available.
valuation.qualification: Result, share reconciliation, and stipulated P/E remain unresolved.

market_behavior.conclusion: MU lagged QQQ over 63 sessions despite a recent rebound, with higher realized volatility.

policy_exposure.conclusion: Tariff/trade restrictions are a conditional cost, delay, and demand channel.
policy_exposure.qualification: No direct product/geography mapping or impact is supplied.

relative_preference.qualification: Provisional EPS, non-comparable valuation, and adverse historical path risk preclude it.

QQQ.thesis: QQQ offers dated diversification across roughly 103 holdings while retaining material direct NVDA and MU overlap. It was above supplied moving averages but lagged SPY over the matched 63-session window; its sponsor aggregate valuation cannot be converted into a company-style EPS/P/E scenario.
QQQ.counter_thesis: Issuer-specific diversification does not insulate QQQ from shared AI, policy, or discount-rate shocks, and the record provides no fund operating scenario or factor sensitivity.
assumptions: Holdings are the September 18 sponsor view; aggregate P/E is August 31 sponsor methodology.
No synthetic ETF earnings scenario is inferred.

review_conditions.description: Review sponsor holdings and aggregate characteristics on the next dated release; changed weights or methodology alter the overlap/valuation description.
A split-adjusted completed close below frozen 50-session average 709.9512 would weaken the intermediate trend while the supplied path already lagged SPY.

QQQ.valuation: No ETF scenario grid is appropriate. Sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08 as of 2026-08-31, with 103 holdings reported as of 2026-09-10. This aggregate measure has sponsor methodology and is not comparable to stipulated company P/E inputs or a fund fair value.
QQQ.etf_lookthrough: September 18 holdings reported NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%, with 99.859505% reported equity weight; excluded cash/futures/synthetic and unknown-weight positions mean no renormalization or current exposure inference.

business.qualification: Composition is dated and incomplete for non-equity positions.

valuation.conclusion: A dated sponsor aggregate P/E is available.
valuation.qualification: It is not comparable to company stress multiples or a fair-value estimate.

market_behavior.conclusion: QQQ lagged SPY over the supplied 63-session window.

policy_exposure.conclusion: Dated issuer weights create indirect policy transmission.
policy_exposure.qualification: No fund loss coefficient or current constituent mapping is available.

relative_preference.conclusion: No QQQ preference over either issuer is established.
relative_preference.qualification: Diversification is structural, but no comparable fund operating scenario or valuation framework exists.
